engagement_title: Meridian Academy Lesson 4 rebuild: cut a forty seven minute single take into a lesson people finish, bring five mixed ratio screencasts to one frame, recover the crest off a printed certificate, and hand back the caption system and the catalogue stills editable
vertical: Professional education, a four person self paced online academy selling an operations and analytics course to working adults (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com 'Online Course / Explainer Video Editor' post carried in the ledger, whose verbatim intent is that an editor is handed a recorded talking head lecture plus slide decks and screen recordings and must cut them into a clean professional lesson video, trimming filler and dead air, cutting between the presenter and the on screen material, adding title cards, lower thirds and on screen key point captions, and exporting a 16:9 course master plus a course catalogue thumbnail. That client wanted a lesson, not a clip. REASONABLY ENRICHED and REPOSITIONED for connector reality, which changes what the honest fuller commission is in three ways. The connector cannot composite a lower third onto a video track, so the key point caption system is delivered as a genuinely editable card set on the HTML to Express surface, which is what the real client actually needed anyway (their previous editor handed back a flattened picture they could not change per cohort). The connector cannot trim to a timestamp, so the tightening is done by the shortening route, which chooses its own retained set and therefore has to be inspected rather than trusted. And the academy's crest survives only on printed certificates, so the identity is recovered off a photograph rather than reinvented. No real academy, person or trademark is named; the line is laundered to the coined fictional Meridian Academy, and Freelancer.com is only the sourcing platform.
client_one_liner: Lesson 4 is forty seven minutes of me talking in one take with five screen recordings that are all different shapes, it is where our learners stop, and we relist the course in January.
client_brief:
Meridian Academy, Lesson 4 rebuild

We are four people in Portland. We sell one self paced course, Operations Analytics for Working Managers, at two hundred and ninety dollars. Our learners are thirty to fifty, doing this at nine at night after their own jobs. There are eight lessons. Seven of them do fine. Lesson 4 is where people stop.

Here is what Lesson 4 actually is. I recorded it in one sitting at my desk, forty seven minutes, no retakes, and I ramble. Somewhere in the middle I walk through the reconciliation model, which is the whole reason the lesson exists, and I play back a recording of a real customer call as the worked example. Around that there are five screen recordings I made separately on two different machines, and they are all different shapes and sizes because I never thought about it.

What we need. A tightened version of me that a tired person will actually finish, with the audio cleaned up so it stops sounding like a spare room. The screen segments brought to one consistent shape so the lesson does not jump about. A set of key point captions that sit over the video as cards, and we want those as a working file, because we rewrite them every cohort and the last editor left us a flattened picture we could not touch.

We also need stills for the catalogue: the course tile, the smaller card in the browse grid, and one of me for the instructor line. All pulled from this lesson, all looking like one lesson.

One more thing. Our crest now exists only on the completion certificates we had printed two years ago. The design file is gone. We would like it back as artwork we can use at any size.

Our look should be plain and adult. We are not a bootcamp and we are not a university. Please write down what you did and anything we should know before we re record.
price_band_and_audience: A two hundred and ninety dollar self paced professional course sold to working adults aged thirty to fifty who are paying with their own money and watching late at night. The band is load bearing. At this price the learner expects a competent, quiet, adult production: legible screen material, a voice that sounds like a person in a room rather than a podcast studio, restrained type, and a thumbnail that promises a working skill rather than a transformation. The same lesson at a nineteen dollar impulse band would correctly be cut fast and bright with arrows, zooms, high contrast captions and a face reaction thumbnail, and shipping that treatment here reads as content marketing and triggers refunds from managers who bought a tool. Push the other way into a university register, slow pacing, a serif institutional crest and a lecture hall thumbnail, and it misprices a course a person finishes on a laptop in four evenings. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Practical skills for people who already have a job.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021 in Portland, Oregon. A four person team running one course.
brand_identity.about: Meridian Academy sells a single self-paced program, Operations Analytics for Working Managers, at two hundred and ninety dollars. Our learners are thirty to fifty, mid-career, watching lessons late at night after their own workday. We are not a bootcamp and we are not a university. We teach one useful thing well and we respect the viewer's time and intelligence.
brand_identity.audience: Working managers aged thirty to fifty, paying with their own money, fitting the course around a full-time job. They want a working skill, not a transformation story, and they distrust anything that feels like marketing.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-market. A two hundred and ninety dollar considered purchase. The register sits between an impulse-priced tutorial and a formal institution: competent, quiet, self-funded professional development.
brand_identity.typography: One restrained type system across every card and still: a plain, legible workhorse for body and captions, paired with a slightly more characterful face for titles. No display gimmicks, generous size for late-night laptop reading.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, warm, matter of fact. Speaks to a peer, not a beginner. Short sentences, no hype, no exclamation. The tone of a good colleague explaining something over coffee.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Brand files are largely gone. When we changed studios the original crest design file was lost, and the mark now survives only on the completion certificates we had printed two years ago: an enclosed laurel ring with small caps type set inside it and a rule beneath, in one deep ink on cream stock. We would like it recovered as artwork we can use at any size. No usable logo vector, colour spec sheet or type licence exists on our side.
brand_identity.values: Respect for the learner's time, honesty about what the course does and does not cover, and production that is clear and quiet rather than loud.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_lesson4_lecture.mp4
assets_supplied.kind: A single take talking head lecture, forty seven minutes, 1920x1080, the instructor seated at a home office desk with a window behind her right shoulder, recorded on a webcam with a desk microphone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Lesson 4, one sitting, no retakes. I ramble. The reconciliation walkthrough is in the middle somewhere and there is a bit where I play back a customer call as the example."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The passage the lesson exists for is delivered quietly, slowly and with the instructor looking down at her notes, while the three loudest and most animated passages in the take are an aside about her dog, a coughing fit and a long apology for the noise outside. Any automatic shortening pass therefore has strong reasons to keep the wrong material and drop the walkthrough, and it will return a tight, watchable, entirely plausible cut either way. Separately, the played back customer call is not the instructor's own voice arriving through the desk microphone, so a speech clean up pass treats it as room noise and suppresses it, leaving four minutes in which she narrates a recording nobody can hear.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_lesson4_screencasts/ (5 recordings)
assets_supplied.kind: Five screen recordings made separately on two machines: three at 1440x900 from a laptop, two at 2560x1600 from an external display, covering the spreadsheet model, a dashboard, a report export and two slide sequences.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The screen bits. Two different machines, and I know they are all different shapes."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: None of the five is 16:9, and the figures the lecture verbally points at (the formula bar on the spreadsheet recordings, the footer totals on the slide recordings) live in the bottom band of the native frame, which is exactly what a fill route to 16:9 removes while returning a clean looking screencast at full success. The two capture resolutions also mean the common 16:9 frame is governed by the smallest source rather than the largest, and one of the laptop recordings sits below the frame the other four could comfortably reach.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_captions.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The key point caption sheet the instructor's assistant assembled: fourteen rows of timecode, caption text and the on screen term being defined.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The captions we want on screen. Fourteen of them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the fourteen rows are full definitions running four to five times the length of the other eleven, so a card measure that suits the short rows does not spill on the long ones, it simply stops rendering and truncates mid definition at the card edge. Two further rows share an identical timecode with different text, a duplicate left in during assembly, and the lesson's central term is spelled two different ways across the sheet.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_certificate_print.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A handheld photograph of a printed completion certificate lying on a table, carrying the academy crest in one deep ink on cream stock: an enclosed laurel ring with small caps type set inside it and a rule beneath.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The crest only exists on these now. The design file went when we changed studios."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup on a photographed substrate, so a prompt naming the certificate returns the paper rather than the ink, a prompt naming the whole crest returns the laurel ring while silently dropping the inner type and the rule, and background removal on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The ink also runs close to the stock in value across the lower left of the sheet where the table lamp falls off.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_lesson4_outline.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The approved lesson outline as written before recording, six numbered beats with the learning objective for each.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The recorded take covers five of the six beats. Beat four was dropped on the day and never re recorded, and nothing in the outline, the filenames or the caption sheet says so, while two of the fourteen captions are written against that missing beat.

acceptance_bar: The tightened lecture still teaches the lesson. The reconciliation walkthrough, which is the reason the lesson exists, survives into the delivered cut, and no delivered cut is shorter than the material it needs to carry.
The delivered lesson master is audible on laptop speakers, and nothing the lecture teaches with is missing from it. A master that is clean because content was removed is not clean.
All five screen segments arrive at one consistent 16:9 frame, and no segment loses any region the lecture verbally refers to.
No delivered video or still exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it came from. A segment that reaches the common frame by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The three catalogue stills read as one lesson: one white point, one black point, one treatment of the window light, and each cut to its own catalogue ratio rather than one still resized three times.
Every caption card renders its whole caption. A card that ends mid sentence at the card edge is not a card.
The caption set matches the delivered cut and the delivered lesson, with no caption pointing at material that is not in either.
The caption cards and the thumbnail arrive in ONE working file the academy can retype and re lay themselves, with every word live text and the crest live vector, not a picture of a layout.

The crest is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and still legible as the same crest at the size it reproduces on a browse tile.
One type system across every card and every still, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note states what was applied to the lecture and to each screen segment, every resize any tool reported, the reconciliation between the outline, the captions and what is actually in the take, and anything that could not be delivered.

adobe_surfaces.tools: video_metadata, video_render_frame, media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole moving half of the commission. It reads what the five screencasts and the lecture actually are before any frame is chosen, cleans the speech on a take recorded in a spare room, shortens a forty seven minute single take toward a length a tired learner finishes, brings five native capture ratios to one common frame without enlarging any of them, and pulls the catalogue frames out of the finished cut. Every one of these tools returns a result that looks correct, so the surface is only usable if each output is inspected by rendering frames from it and summarising it, rather than by reading the success response.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every still decision. It brings three frames pulled from one take to one catalogue look with a masked correction where the window behind the instructor's shoulder blows out, cuts each still to its own catalogue ratio while reading the returned tradeoffs rather than the success message, and recovers the crest at ink level off a photographed certificate with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The caption card system and the course thumbnail as one native editable document at mixed canvas sizes, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout and the only route to the working file the academy explicitly asked for. Every still must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the crest goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the caption cards, the thumbnail and the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on plain and adult rather than bootcamp or university. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name has to be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the academy does not have, a quiet evening desk still for the browse card ground, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the sign off board the four of them review the thumbnail candidates and caption cards from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cut, the segments and the audio are video work; the caption cards and the thumbnail have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the academy edits them every cohort and nothing else in the connector composes free form layout. The brief already pins the destination, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the lecture, the five screencasts, the certificate photograph, the caption sheet and the outline, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that thirty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which recording.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read the metadata on the lecture and on all five screencasts, and render sample frames across each of them.
trajectory.judgement: The client says the screencasts are different shapes; the metadata says which shapes, and the frames say what is actually inside those shapes and where on the frame it sits. The common frame cannot be chosen before both are known, and the smallest source governs it because nothing may be enlarged.
trajectory.produces: A per file inventory of native frame size and ratio, plus rendered frames showing where each recording carries its content.

trajectory.action: Summarise the lecture to establish what is actually said and in what order, and reconcile that against the six beat outline and the fourteen caption rows.
trajectory.judgement: The outline is what was planned and the caption sheet is what someone wrote afterwards. Only the recording settles what the lesson contains, and reading the three against each other is slower than trusting the outline but is the only thing that catches a beat that was never recorded.
trajectory.produces: A spine of the take by topic, and a reconciliation note against the outline and the caption sheet.

trajectory.action: Clean the speech on the lecture, then summarise the cleaned master and set that summary beside the summary of the raw take.
trajectory.judgement: Speech clean up is the only audio tool available and its whole method is to keep the speaker and suppress what is not the speaker. Comparing the two summaries is the only readout the connector offers on what the clean up decided was not the speaker.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned lesson master and a side by side account of what each summary reports.

trajectory.action: Tighten the lecture toward a length a tired learner finishes, then render frames across the result and summarise it.
trajectory.judgement: The shortening route chooses its own retained set and offers no way to nominate a passage. Whether the lesson survived the tightening is not in the response; it is in the frames and the summary of the output.
trajectory.produces: A tightened lecture cut, plus a frame walk and a summary of what that cut actually contains.

trajectory.action: Fix the common 16:9 frame from the inventory, then reframe all five screencasts to it and render frames from each RESIZED output at the moments the lecture points at figures.
trajectory.judgement: The frame is set by the smallest source, not by the largest, because nothing may be enlarged. And a reframe that crops rather than fits is a decision about which band of the screen to lose, which can only be judged against the moments the lecture verbally refers to.
trajectory.produces: Five segments at one common 16:9 frame, each with rendered evidence from the resized output at its cited moments.

trajectory.action: Pull the three catalogue frames out of the tightened cut: the course tile hero, the browse card still and the instructor line portrait.
trajectory.judgement: Frames pulled from the tightened cut are the ones that match what the learner will see; frames pulled from the raw take may show material that is no longer in the lesson.
trajectory.produces: Three source frames at the video's own scale, with the timecode each came from recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview the three frames, fix one catalogue target off the cleanest of them, and bring all three to it with their own calls, including a confined correction where the window behind the instructor's shoulder blows out.
trajectory.judgement: Three frames from one take are still three different exposures because she moves. One batched identical parameter set is exactly wrong; the target is a set, not three good stills. Naming the window's own visual properties takes the window, naming the wall behind her takes the wall.
trajectory.produces: Three graded stills to one look with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut each still to its own catalogue ratio, reading the returned tradeoffs and detection readings on every crop rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: A course tile, a browse card and an instructor line are three different crops of three different frames, not one still at three sizes. The tradeoffs object is the only channel that reports what the tool did to the dimensions and it carries no warning language.
trajectory.produces: Three catalogue stills at their own ratios with every returned tradeoff recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the crest off the certificate photograph: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink and not the stock, which polarity to trace, and whether the ring, the inner type and the rule can be taken in one selection or need separate passes composited. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed laurel ring.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent crest, with the passes that produced it recorded.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the quiet evening desk still, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the catalogue target rather than the prettiest thumbnail, and keep it plain enough that it does not outshine the instructor's own stills. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a two hundred and ninety dollar course for a thirty to fifty year old manager. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Resolve the caption sheet against the delivered cut: settle the shared timecode, unify the term that is spelled two ways, decide what happens to the captions written against material that is not in the lesson, and set the card measure the long definitions have to live inside.
trajectory.judgement: A caption pointing at something the learner will not see is worse than no caption. The long rows are the ones that decide the measure, and choosing the measure from the short rows is the comfortable wrong answer.
trajectory.produces: A final caption set with the reconciliation written down.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the caption cards at the video frame size and the thumbnail at its own canvas size, inline the stills as image data, place the crest as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A still left as a URL is not a still, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how a caption stays legible over moving footage without shouting at an adult learner.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole card system and the thumbnail, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every other canvas.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit of the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the sign off board, add the thumbnail candidates, the catalogue stills and the caption card renders within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector crest is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the academy knows what to fix before they re record.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the tightened lecture still contains the lesson. The shortening route accepts a source and a target length and nothing else: it chooses its own retained set, offers no way to nominate or protect a passage, and returns a tight, coherent, entirely watchable cut. In this take the reconciliation walkthrough, which is the reason the lesson exists, is delivered quietly and slowly with the instructor looking down at her notes, while the three most energetic passages in forty seven minutes are an aside about her dog, a coughing fit and an apology for street noise. Which of those the pass keeps is a property of this recording and is reported nowhere in the response. It is visible only by rendering frames across the output and summarising the output, and then reading that against the spine of the raw take.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the tool exposes no control over selection and the client cannot be asked to re record. The brief says only that she rambles and that the walkthrough is somewhere in the middle, which is a description of the source, not a statement about what the tightening will drop. And the response is not the same call again: it is a different route, deciding whether to tighten from the raw take or the cleaned master, whether to give the pass a longer target so the quiet passage is inside its budget, or whether the automatic route is wrong for this lecture and the highlight has to be built differently and the difference declared.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the tightening for the lecture, re derive the cut through the chosen route, re render frames across the new output and re summarise it, and then re reconcile the caption set and the catalogue frame timecodes against whatever the new cut actually contains.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A tight, clean, professional feeling Lesson 4 that has had the reconciliation walkthrough removed and keeps the dog, delivered to the one lesson in the course where learners already stop, with every tool response reporting success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which band of each screen recording the common frame takes. None of the five is 16:9, and the figures the lecture points at live in the bottom band of the native capture: the formula bar on the spreadsheet recordings, the footer totals on the slide recordings. A reframe that fills the target ratio removes exactly that band and hands back a clean, sharp, well composed screencast at full success, with no indication of what left the frame. Nothing in the metadata says where the content sits, and a frame rendered from the SOURCE looks correct because the content is still there. Only a frame rendered from the RESIZED output, at the moment the lecture verbally refers to a figure, shows the row is gone. Which of the five this bites, and how hard, differs per recording because the two machines placed their chrome differently.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The reframe is the only route to a consistent frame, so it cannot be ordered around, and there is no read ahead that reports what a ratio change will discard. Nothing states it either: the brief asks only that the segments stop jumping about, and the acceptance line about not losing a referenced region is the client's standing requirement, not a disclosure that a reframe eats a band. The response is a different route rather than a repeat, choosing the fit behaviour on the affected recordings so the content survives inside the common frame, or setting a different common frame that the smallest source can still reach without enlargement, which then re opens the frame decision for all five.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re choose the common frame from the inventory, re run the affected segments through the other route, re render frames from each new resized output at the cited moments, and re check every returned resize report so that no segment reached the frame by being enlarged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Five consistent, sharp looking screen segments in which the instructor says look at the formula bar and there is no formula bar, shipped to the exact lesson the academy already knows learners abandon.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the caption cards are built on. A caption sitting over moving footage is authored the natural way as a frosted translucent bar behind the words, or as words carrying an outline and a layered drop so they hold over any frame. The importer discards a backdrop treatment entirely, discards an outline on text so completely that outlined type becomes a fully transparent colour and vanishes, discards a text shadow, and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, and it does all of that while returning a successful export with no warning of any kind. The document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so if the thumbnail is canvas one, every caption canvas can be checked through no channel except the returned per canvas markup. Whether the caption still reads as a caption, or has become invisible words on a flat panel, is knowable only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The drop happens at import and the import is the last step, so no ordering reaches it earlier, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which no response reports and no checklist enumerates. The brief asks for captions the academy can edit and says nothing about construction. The response is to build the legibility differently, as an opaque or single layer panel that is part of the layout rather than an effect applied to it, and then re judge whether the caption still sits quietly enough for an adult course, which re opens the card design rather than repeating the export.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the caption construction, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard, checking each caption's colour and each card's surviving panel.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A caption card set delivered as the editable working file the academy specifically asked for, in which the captions are invisible on every canvas after the first, with the export having reported success throughout and the thumbnail on canvas one looking perfect.

deliverables.name: Lesson 4 delivered lesson set
deliverables.spec: The tightened lecture at 16:9 that still contains the reconciliation walkthrough, five screen segments brought to one common 16:9 frame with nothing the lecture refers to lost from any of them, and a cleaned lesson audio master that is audible on laptop speakers without having had teaching content suppressed out of it. Every output at or below the pixel dimensions of the source it came from, with the resize report for each recorded.

deliverables.name: Meridian catalogue stills
deliverables.spec: Three distinct frames pulled from the delivered cut, the course tile hero, the browse grid card and the instructor line portrait, brought to one catalogue look with one white point, one black point and one treatment of the window light, each cut to its own catalogue ratio, plus one licensed camera scale desk frame graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log including why each frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Recovered Meridian crest
deliverables.spec: The compound crest recovered from a photograph of a printed certificate as placeable scalable vector geometry on a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, the laurel ring, the inner small caps type and the rule all present, and still legible as the same crest at the size it actually reproduces on a browse tile.

deliverables.name: Caption card system and course thumbnail, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying the reconciled caption cards at the video frame size and the course thumbnail at its own canvas size, with every caption as live retypable text in one licensed type system, the crest as real vector shapes, every still carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and no caption truncated at a card edge. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half the academy rebuilds from each cohort.

deliverables.name: Handover note and sign off board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was applied to the lecture and to each screen segment, every resize any tool reported and the file it applied to, the reconciliation between the six beat outline, the fourteen caption rows and what the take actually contains, what the audio clean up cost and how that was handled, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, and anything the academy should fix before they re record. Paired with a persistent shareable sign off board carrying the thumbnail candidates, the catalogue stills and the caption card renders with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: Every delivered video and still is at or below the pixel dimensions of the source it derives from, and all five screen segments share one identical frame size and ratio.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the frame dimensions of every delivered file and compare each against the source named for it in the manifest, then compare the five segments against each other.

verifiers_auto.text: No resize report captured in the run carries an enlargement entry, and every reduction entry is transcribed in the handover note.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the reported tradeoff and resize records captured from every video and image call against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The delivered lecture cut is shorter than the source take and no delivered cut is empty or truncated at its tail.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the duration of the delivered cut against the source duration, and render frames at the head and tail of the delivered cut.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered crest's SVG has a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned the expected number of canvases, each keeping its own declared canvas size.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and the per canvas width and height in the export response.

verifiers_auto.text: No caption text in the exported markup resolved to a fully transparent colour, and no still resolved to the importer's placeholder image.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per canvas markup for transparent colour values on text nodes and for one by one placeholder image data.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_auto.text: The caption card count in the exported document equals the reconciled caption count in the note, and no caption string in the markup is a prefix of its row in the reconciled sheet.
verifiers_auto.how: Count caption canvases in the export response and compare each rendered caption string against the reconciled sheet character for character.

verifiers_auto.text: The sign off board exists with the expected item count and an empty failed items list after the final call.
verifiers_auto.how: Read boardId and the addedEntityIds and failedItems arrays from the board responses.

verifiers_human.text: The tightened lecture still teaches Lesson 4. The reconciliation walkthrough is present and coherent, and the cut does not end on an aside.
verifiers_human.how: Watch the delivered cut end to end against the spine of the raw take and the lesson outline.

verifiers_human.text: The delivered lesson master is audible on laptop speakers and the played back worked example is still there and still intelligible.
verifiers_human.how: Listen to the master at the passage the instructor narrates the recording, on laptop speakers rather than headphones.

verifiers_human.text: Every figure the lecture points at is on screen in the segment it belongs to.
verifiers_human.how: Play each segment at the moments the lecture verbally refers to a number and look for the region that carries it.

verifiers_human.text: The three catalogue stills read as one lesson rather than three frames from one video.
verifiers_human.how: Place the three side by side at catalogue scale and judge white point, black point and window treatment as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The crest still reads as the same crest at browse tile size, with the ring, the inner type and the rule intact.
verifiers_human.how: View the crest at its reproduction size on the tile and on the card, not at full canvas.

verifiers_human.text: Every caption card is legible over the footage it sits on and shows its whole caption.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported document, look at every canvas in Express, and read each caption to its end.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a two hundred and ninety dollar adult professional course, not as a bootcamp and not as a university.
verifiers_human.how: Judge pacing, caption tone, type scale and thumbnail promise against the stated band and learner.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the academy something they did not already know, including everything that could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that every reconciliation and every limitation is named.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are video work and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and only one produces the working file the academy asked for.
Whether the tightening runs from the raw take or from the cleaned master, and what target length gives the lesson room to survive.
What the speech clean up cost the lesson, and whether the delivered master is the cleaned one, the raw one, or the cleaned one with the loss declared.
The common screen frame: set by the smallest source rather than the largest, and whether each recording reaches it by fitting or by cropping.
Which timecodes the three catalogue frames come from, given that a frame from the raw take may show material no longer in the lesson.
Whether the outline's six beats, the fourteen captions and the recorded take describe the same lesson, and how to say so when they do not.
What happens to the two captions written against a beat that was never recorded.
The caption card measure, which is decided by the three long definitions and not by the eleven short ones.

Selection wording on the certificate: naming the certificate takes the stock, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the crest, and background removal on an enclosed laurel ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the crest can be taken in one selection or needs the ring, the inner type and the rule composited from separate passes.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a working manager watching at nine at night, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How loud the caption cards are allowed to be. At this band restraint is the design, and a high contrast arrow heavy caption is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of an online course. IDENTITY: this is this instructor, in this take, teaching this reconciliation model, and the crest must be RECOVERED off a printed certificate rather than reinvented, because a regenerated crest is a different academy's crest and a regenerated instructor is not the person the learner bought the course from. SPEC: five screen recordings at two native capture ratios have to arrive at one identical frame with no enlargement and no loss of the regions the lecture points at, a forty seven minute take has to become a lesson a person finishes, and the audio has to survive a clean up that was never asked to preserve a played back recording. None of that is producible by generation and none of it can be checked on a generated image. EDITABILITY: the caption system is defined by being editable, since the academy rewrites the captions every cohort and their last editor's flattened picture is exactly the failure they are paying to escape. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did the tightening keep the walkthrough, did the reframe take the formula bar, did the caption survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account) or is on the standing doable list, five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO: video_metadata, video_render_frame, media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut and video_resize are the sanctioned Premiere set; the task uses quick cut only to SHORTEN and video_resize only to re aspect within source scale, and never asks for a trim to a timestamp, a format conversion or an enlargement. The checkpoints rest on the material behaviour of those routes rather than on any undocumented feature: the shortening route exposes no selection control, so its retained set is knowable only from rendered frames and a summary of the output; the reframe exposes no readout of what a ratio change discards, so it is knowable only from frames rendered off the RESIZED output. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls, and the crest chain rests on the documented substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the compound mark partial selection, the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the third checkpoint rests on four separately verified silent drops: backdrop-filter dropped, -webkit-text-stroke dropped so stroked text becomes a fully transparent colour, text-shadow dropped and multi layer box-shadow hard truncated to layer one, all at HTTP success, with the rendition documented as PAGE 1 ONLY. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined stills pass the 70 KB threshold immediately, and no photograph is ever left as a URL because URLs render as empty grey boxes. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, including a browser proving licensed faces load, and the non standard numeric weights and slug only CSS rules are enforced. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing onto video, no OCR, no text to image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
